title: The grammar
intro: Vim commands are sentences: an operator (d delete, c change, y yank) followed by a motion. Any motion you know works after any operator. Watch the strip at the top as you type.

levels.title: Delete a word
levels.brief: Delete the word this. dw deletes from the cursor to the start of the next word.
levels.hint: d then w. The trailing space goes with it.

levels.title: Change a word
levels.brief: Turn this into that. cw deletes the word and enters Insert mode, so you can type the replacement.
levels.hint: cw keeps the space after the word. That is a deliberate Vim quirk.

levels.title: Two words
levels.brief: Delete two and three. A count between operator and motion repeats the motion.
levels.hint: d2w and 2dw do the same thing.

levels.title: To the end
levels.brief: Delete everything from the cursor to the end of the line. D is a shortcut for d$.
levels.hint: d$ costs two keys, D costs one.

levels.title: Change to end
levels.brief: Correct the number. C changes from the cursor to the end of the line.

levels.title: Copy a line
levels.brief: Duplicate the line. yy yanks (copies) the line, p puts it below.

levels.title: Three lines
levels.brief: Delete the first three lines with a count on dd.

levels.title: Count times count
levels.brief: Delete six words. A count before the operator and a count before the motion multiply.
start: w1 w2 w3 w4 w5 w6 w7
levels.hint: 2d3w is two times three words. d6w also works.

levels.title: Lines downward
levels.brief: Delete the first two lines with one operator and one motion. dj deletes this line and the one below.
levels.hint: Vertical motions are linewise: the whole lines go.

levels.title: Yank to end
levels.brief: Make the line read copy thisthis. y$ yanks to the end of the line, $ moves there, p puts after the cursor.
levels.hint: Yanking does not move the cursor when the motion goes forward.
